title: Project Overview
description: Start with README.md to identify the current PCIe-8332 UDP backend, its independent client and the hardware-free regression suite. The repository also retains direct-NIC tools and an older Unreal protocol, so the tour first follows the current backend before comparing those separate paths.

title: Deployment And Configuration
description: Following the README, the backend guide and example configuration show which settings belong to the server: endpoint, authentication, heartbeat timeout, APS card options and endpoint sensors. The Windows launchers select tray or headless operation, while requirements.txt supplies the tray dependencies. This establishes the operating environment before tracing startup code.

title: Backend Startup And Shutdown
description: backend.py is the current application entry point: it validates the settings from the previous step, configures rotating logs and starts MotorService with UDPServer. Tray mode launches the control interface as a separate process, while headless mode hosts the same service without that interface. Both routes close the server and hardware owner when the process exits.

title: Shared Motion Vocabulary
description: Before examining startup's two services, read control_common.py for the shared Device, Move, MotionCommand and error types. Its validation and adapter exclusivity support both current and legacy controllers, and its locked queue replaces pending targets while preserving accumulated relative intent. These types explain what the network layer requests and what the hardware worker consumes.
languageLesson: Frozen dataclasses represent immutable records, and a context manager places lock release in a finally block so errors cannot strand hardware ownership.

title: Versioned UDP Contract
description: The v1 protocol translates the motion vocabulary into explicit hello, scan, enable, target, heartbeat, disable and release requests. UDPServer enforces an exclusive session, authentication, bounded request deduplication and increasing control sequences, while run IDs isolate target and heartbeat traffic from previous runs. The protocol guide also explains snapshot ordering, so retries and reordered datagrams can be understood separately from physical motion.

title: Service Worker And Watchdog
description: MotorService receives the validated requests from UDPServer and coordinates scanning, enabling, active targets, stopping and fault state. A single-worker executor owns hardware access; the watchdog requests a stop after heartbeat expiry and schedules idle sensor reads through that same worker. Status snapshots cross the thread boundary as copied data, and failures remain latched until an explicit scan.
languageLesson: ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) serializes queued hardware operations; locks protect shared service state while events communicate cooperative stop requests.

title: APS Card And Topology
description: The service's default hardware owner is PCIe8332Controller in aps_backend.py. Its ctypes bindings load the APS DLL and validate the SV635N topology, axis mapping, position units and motor direction before enabling selected axes. The card generates the point-to-point trajectories, making Python responsible for validated commands and feedback rather than EtherCAT cycle generation.
languageLesson: ctypes structures and explicit argument/return types mirror the native SDK ABI; matching pointer sizes and data layouts matters before any hardware call.

title: Endpoint Protection And Cleanup
description: Building on the validated axes, the APS controller interprets configured extension and retraction feedback and permits movement away from an active endpoint while rejecting movement toward it. Missing feedback and conflicting endpoints participate in preflight and runtime fault checks, and a stopped target does not resume automatically when a sensor clears. Cleanup stops owned axes, verifies servo disable and restores temporary parameters before MotorService declares a clean stop.

title: Independent Client SDK
description: With server behavior established, MotorClient packages the same v1 contract into a standard-library SDK that imports no hardware libraries. It manages retried ACK requests, session ownership, run-scoped targets, independent heartbeats and telemetry ordering. The wire helpers and command-line example show how an external program uses that boundary and disables its run during cleanup.

title: UDP Control Interface
description: The Tk debug interface builds on MotorClient to select devices, scan, enable and stream coalesced slider targets. It renders axis and endpoint feedback and uses a dedicated executor for stop requests so an ordinary ACK wait cannot hold them up. Its separate entry point and endpoint-only configuration preserve the deployment boundary introduced by the backend tray launcher.

title: Hardware-Free Regression Evidence
description: The test suites verify the complete path just traced using fake APS APIs, injected EtherCAT controllers and loopback UDP. They exercise endpoint protection, stop and restoration, replay and retry handling, heartbeat expiry, UI feedback and single-thread hardware ownership. Deployment tests also check that the client runs without backend packages and that the backend imports without frontend packages.

title: Legacy Paths And Compatibility
description: Finally, compare the current architecture with core.py and app.py, which retain direct-NIC pysoem discovery and local CiA402 motion. platform_control.py hosts the older three-axis bridge used by the Unreal component and requires explicit bridge startup. Its motor-angle messages are incompatible with the current v1 UDP RPC backend, so the Unreal reference cannot be pointed at that server unchanged.
